questions.question: What is a system boundary?
choices: A defined separation between a system and its surroundings
A guarantee that the system exchanges nothing
A line that must follow a national border
A physical wall required around every system

questions.question: What is an input to an environmental system?
choices: Material or energy leaving it
Material or energy entering the chosen system
The total amount already stored only
A process that cannot be measured

questions.question: What is a system stock?
choices: Only the speed of material movement
A one-time label for a species
An amount accumulated within a system
The number of possible models

questions.question: What is a positive feedback?
choices: Any change that improves an outcome for people
A process that opposes the initial disturbance
A process with no influence on later conditions
A process that amplifies an initial change

questions.question: What is a negative feedback?
choices: A process that opposes an initial change
Any change that produces an undesirable outcome
A process that amplifies the initial disturbance
A transfer that changes no other process

questions.question: What is a time lag in a system response?
choices: The maximum possible size of a response
A delay between a cause and an observable effect
A response occurring before its cause
A difference only in the units used

questions.question: What is dynamic equilibrium in a reservoir's material balance?
choices: All transfers permanently stop
Inputs rise while outputs remain zero
Inputs and outputs balance while transfers continue
Every stored particle is motionless

questions.question: Why does a positive feedback not mean a desirable outcome?
choices: Positive means all organisms benefit equally
Feedback signs are based only on opinions
Amplification always removes every risk
Positive describes amplification, not value or benefit

questions.question: How can loss of reflective snow contribute to further warming?
choices: Darker surfaces absorb more sunlight, encouraging more snow loss
Darker surfaces reflect more sunlight than snow
Snow loss leaves energy absorption unchanged
Melting always increases surface reflectivity

questions.question: How can increased plant uptake of carbon dioxide oppose an initial rise in carbon dioxide under suitable conditions?
choices: It increases carbon dioxide while opposing the rise
It removes some of the added carbon dioxide
It guarantees carbon dioxide reaches zero
It stops carbon from moving through organisms

questions.question: Why can a system appear stable while large flows continue?
choices: A steady stock proves inputs and outputs are zero
All environmental systems exchange no energy
Balanced inputs and outputs can maintain a steady stock
Any material flow must increase the stock

questions.question: Why can a delayed response complicate management?
choices: Effects occur only while an action is still taking place
Delayed effects can be ignored when choosing actions
Time lags guarantee there is no causal relationship
Present actions may have effects not visible immediately

questions.question: What is an environmental threshold?
choices: A condition beyond which a system's behavior can change substantially
A maximum instrument reading unrelated to system behavior
A condition that is identical in all ecosystems
A point beyond which measurement is impossible

questions.question: Why are feedbacks important in environmental models?
choices: They guarantee that models have no uncertainty
They connect changes to processes that modify later changes
They replace the need for observational evidence
They ensure every response is proportional and immediate

questions.question: Why can changing a system boundary change an assessment?
choices: It changes conservation of matter within the same process
It makes excluded effects cease to exist physically
It changes which transfers and effects are counted
It guarantees that a narrower boundary captures more effects

questions.question: A pond receives 50 L per minute and loses 30 L per minute, with other flows negligible. What is its storage change?
choices: A decrease of 20 L per minute
An increase of 80 L per minute
No change
An increase of 20 L per minute

questions.question: Higher temperature causes more ice melt, and the resulting darker surface increases warming. What feedback is described?
choices: Positive feedback
Negative feedback
No feedback
A permanently closed material cycle

questions.question: A population grows, increasing competition that lowers its growth rate. What feedback is described?
choices: Positive feedback
Negative feedback
No interaction between population and resources
A process making resource supply unlimited

questions.question: A lake's pollutant input falls, but sediments continue releasing old pollution. What helps explain delayed improvement?
choices: All pollution vanishes as soon as inputs decline
Stored pollution can never reenter the water
Stored material and time lags
The decline proves there are no continuing internal flows

questions.question: A model counts emissions during product use but excludes manufacturing. How should its result be interpreted?
choices: It necessarily represents all life-cycle stages
It proves manufacturing has no impacts
It can be compared directly with any differently bounded study
It describes the chosen boundary, not the full product life cycle
